sections.heading: Vector Fields, Conservative Fields & Line Integrals Practice Exercises

questions.q: Consider the vector field \( \mathbf{F}(x,y) = \langle 3x, 2y \rangle \). Evaluate the vector field at the point \( (2, 4) \).
questions.answer:
The vector field is given by \( \mathbf{F}(x,y) = \langle 3x, 2y \rangle \). To evaluate the vector field at the point \( (2, 4) \), we substitute \( x=2 \) and \( y=4 \) into the components of the vector field.

First component: \( 3x = 3(2) = 6 \).
Second component: \( 2y = 2(4) = 8 \).

Therefore, \( \mathbf{F}(2,4) = \langle 6, 8 \rangle \).

questions.q: Consider the vector field \( \mathbf{F}(x, y) = \langle 2x, 3y \rangle \). Which of the following options best represents the vector field at the point (1, 1)?
questions.answer: To find the representation of the vector field \( \mathbf{F}(x, y) = \langle 2x, 3y \rangle \) at a specific point, we substitute the coordinates of the point into the components of the vector field. At the point (1, 1), we have: \( x = 1 \) and \( y = 1 \). Substituting these values into \( \mathbf{F}(x, y) \) gives: \( \mathbf{F}(1, 1) = \langle 2(1), 3(1) \rangle = \langle 2, 3 \rangle \). Therefore, the vector field at the point (1, 1) is \( \langle 2, 3 \rangle \). Option B is incorrect as it represents the position vector at (1,1). Option C is incorrect as it represents the vector field at (2,2). Option D is incorrect as it uses the x-component from (2,y) and the y-component from (x,2).

questions.q: Consider the vector field \( \mathbf{F}(x,y) = \langle 2x+y, x-3y \rangle \). What is the value of the vector field at the point \( (3, -1) \)?
questions.answer:
To find the value of the vector field \( \mathbf{F}(x,y) = \langle 2x+y, x-3y \rangle \) at the point \( (3, -1) \), we substitute \( x=3 \) and \( y=-1 \) into the components of the vector field.

The first component is \( 2x+y = 2(3) + (-1) = 6 - 1 = 5 \).

The second component is \( x-3y = 3 - 3(-1) = 3 + 3 = 6 \).

Therefore, the vector field at \( (3, -1) \) is \( \langle 5, 6 \rangle \).

questions.q: Evaluate \( \int_C x^{2}\,ds \) where \( C \) is the segment from \( \left( 0, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 5, \  12\right) \).
Which vector field is conservative on all of \( \mathbb R^2 \)?
questions.answer: On \( \mathbb R^2 \), \( \langle P,Q\rangle \) is conservative iff \( P_y=Q_x \). For \( \langle e^{y}, x e^{y} \rangle \): \( P_y=e^{y}=Q_x \); each other field has \( P_y\ne Q_x \).

questions.q: Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y^{2}, 2 x \rangle \) along the segment from \( \left( -2, \  -2\right) \) to \( \left( -2, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: Parametrize \( \mathbf r(t)=\langle -2, 5 t - 2 \rangle,\ 0\le t\le1 \). Then \( \int_0^1\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)\,dt=\int\limits_{0}^{1} \left(-20\right)\, dt=-20 \).

questions.q: Evaluate \( \int_C x + y\,ds \) where \( C \) is the segment from \( \left( 0, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 4, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: \( \mathbf r(t)=\langle 4 t, 3 t \rangle,\ ds=5\,dt \). \( \int\limits_{0}^{1} 35 t\, dt \) \( = \) \( \frac{35}{2} \).

questions.q: Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x y, y \rangle \) along the segment from \( \left( 1, \  1\right) \) to \( \left( 1, \  -2\right) \).
questions.answer: Parametrize \( \mathbf r(t)=\langle 1, 1 - 3 t \rangle,\ 0\le t\le1 \). Then \( \int_0^1\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)\,dt=\int\limits_{0}^{1} \left(9 t - 3\right)\, dt=\frac{3}{2} \).
